clue.text: Cave-dweller having year in grotto — led out

indicators.note: the year's letter is put in among the rearranged letters of the other two words
led out suggests letters taken out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A caveman spends a year in a grotto before being led out into daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GROTTO and LED into TROGLODTE, and 'in' puts Y between the D and the T.
explanation.definitionFit: A troglodyte is literally someone who lives in a cave, especially a prehistoric person.

clue.text: What may be said after hit for pop band?

definitions.text: What may be said after hit for pop band?

parts.words: What may be said after hit for pop band?
parts.note: the cry of triumph after landing a punch doubles as the name of a 1990s British boy band

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what a pop group might say after scoring a hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hit' sounds like a chart success, but it is a blow, after which a cartoon hero might shout the band's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation a fighter gives when landing a blow is also the name of a famous Manchester boy band.

clue.text: Comprehensive cover?

definitions.meaning: a protective garment worn over other clothes

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means total or all-inclusive; as a noun it is a loose protective garment worn over clothes.

clue.text: C.S. Lewis, perhaps, or his leading character?

definitions.meaning: a celebrated author, a big name in the world of books
Aslan, the hero of the Narnia books, is a lion in a work of literature

explanation.definitionFit: A famous writer is a celebrity of letters, and Lewis's own hero Aslan is quite literally a big cat in a book.

clue.text: Refined young socialite coming out very happily

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman making her entrance into society
walking on air is to be blissfully happy

explanation.surface: A polished debutante makes her entrance into society in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: ON AIR comes from 'walking on air', meaning very happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes someone suave, polished and elegantly confident in manner.

clue.text: Difficult, with empty tummy, consuming cornet?

indicators.note: one thing consuming another takes it inside itself, so the outer pair wraps the instrument
an empty tummy has lost its contents, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: a cornet is a brass instrument, a kind of horn

explanation.surface: Someone with an empty stomach struggles awkwardly to eat an ice-cream cornet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' reduces tummy to TY, and 'consuming' puts HORN inside: T(HORN)Y. Cornet looks like ice cream but is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is a tricky, prickly one that is hard to handle.

clue.text: Lincoln, familiarly and primarily a murder victim

annotationWithheld.why: Lincoln, familiarly and primarily a murder victim (4): ABE (Lincoln, familiarly) + L (first letter of Lincoln); the word Lincoln does two jobs, as nickname source and as the word whose first letter is taken
annotationWithheld.clue: Lincoln, familiarly and primarily a murder victim

clue.text: Finish ahead following run of successful pots

indicators.note: the word for ahead follows the snooker term in the answer

parts.note: in snooker a break is a series of balls potted in one visit to the table
being up is being ahead in a game

explanation.surface: A snooker player pulls ahead to win after a long scoring sequence of pots.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, a game played on a cloth table, a break is a run of pots in one turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To break up is to end or come to a finish, as a meeting or school term does.

clue.text: Tune in late to get broadcast officer's given

indicators.note: words that get broadcast are scattered abroad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone tunes the radio in late to hear an officer's announcement being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A lieutenant is a commissioned officer rank in the army and navy.

clue.text: Closely watch board with regard to covering bills

indicators.note: the two outer words sit either side of the bills, covering them

parts.note: keep means food and lodging, as in bed and board
on means concerning, as in a talk on history
tabs are bills run up, as at a bar

explanation.surface: A board meeting keeps a close eye on the matter of unpaid bills.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep tabs on someone is an idiom for monitoring them carefully.

clue.text: Only minutes before

parts.note: ere is an old poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Something happened just minutes earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means nothing more than, as in a mere child, so it is a synonym of only.

clue.text: A sweet Bordeaux, initially, say, then whisky

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the wine region's name

parts.note: to utter is to say
Scotch is whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone lists a sweet Bordeaux wine followed by a whisky as drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sweet Bordeaux' looks like a dessert wine, but the definition is just 'A sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle confection made from butter and brown sugar.

clue.text: Start of hymn tune, it grows on one

indicators.note: start of picks out the first letter of the word hymn

parts.note: an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A hymn begins with a tune that grows on the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grows on one' sounds like a tune becoming liked, but it means something growing on your body.
explanation.definitionFit: The strands covering the head and body grow out of a person, cryptically described.

clue.text: A number with food in bag leaving Cape Cod resort

indicators.note: the article, number and food are placed in the net

parts.note: to net something is to bag or catch it
N is the abbreviation for number, as in n terms
tuck is British schoolboy slang for food, especially sweets and snacks

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs a number of snacks in a bag before leaving a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: TUCK is British school slang for food, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: This island off Cape Cod in Massachusetts is a famous summer holiday destination.

clue.text: To lampoon dude seen in one ancient city is in keeping

indicators.note: the whole group of pieces is placed in the word for keeping

parts.note: in someone's keeping means in their care

indicators.note: the dude appears inside the pair of one and the ancient city

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
cat is jazz slang for a man or dude

explanation.surface: A satirist mocks a dandy spotted in an ancient city, which seems fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' sets CAT between I and UR to make ICATUR, and 'is in' puts that inside CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To caricature someone is to mock them by exaggerating their features, which is to lampoon.

clue.text: Grace ill? Could be hypersensitive

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Grace's illness might be a sensitivity reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergic person reacts excessively to substances like pollen, being oversensitive to them.

clue.text: Move at home to intervene

parts.note: a step is a move
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone moves house in order to sort out a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is to involve yourself in a situation, an idiom for intervening.

clue.text: Imprisoned in small hospital unit, suffering from depression

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
to be down is to feel low

explanation.surface: A depressed patient is confined to a small hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: SENT DOWN is British slang for being jailed by a court.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sent down is to be given a prison sentence, so it means imprisoned.

clue.text: Almost transfix a creature with horns

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: to impale is to pierce through, to transfix

explanation.surface: A hunter nearly spears a horned beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of IMPALE, giving IMPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope with long curved horns.

clue.text: Lingo used by northern model

indicators.note: the abbreviation for northern is added to the speech word

parts.note: patter is a specialised jargon or glib talk

explanation.surface: A northern fashion model has a distinctive way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or template to be copied.

clue.text: Carnivore's beginning to poke in ground

indicators.note: the letter goes in the word for ground

parts.note: terrain is ground or land

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of poke

explanation.surface: A meat-eater starts poking around in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The terrapin, a freshwater turtle, eats meat such as fish and insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrapins are meat-eating turtles, feeding on fish, snails and insects.

clue.text: Disgraced MP may make up for way of working

indicators.note: these letters may make a new word when rearranged

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: A disgraced politician might make amends for his methods.
explanation.walkthrough: John Profumo was a British minister who resigned in 1963 over a sex scandal. 'make up' looks like a phrase, but 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: John Profumo was the British War Minister brought down by the Profumo affair in 1963.

clue.text: Rattle around most of Pacific island in car

indicators.note: the jar goes around the shortened island

parts.note: to jar is to rattle or jolt

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Guam is a US island territory in the western Pacific

explanation.surface: A car rattles around a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims GUAM to GUA, and 'around' wraps JAR round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaguar is a British make of luxury car.

clue.text: One travelling from Earth to Saturn, possibly around end of era

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the single letter
possibly signals the letters might form something else
end of picks the final letter of era

explanation.surface: A spaceman journeys from Earth out to Saturn, perhaps over the course of an era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TO SATURN into ASTRONUT, and 'around' puts the A from the end of era between N and U.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a person who travels into space from our planet.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: a breed of dog from China with a blue-black tongue
informal slang for grub or eats

explanation.definitionFit: Chow is both a Chinese dog breed and slang for food.

clue.text: See 1
Took advantage of American edition

explanation.surface: Someone exploited an American edition of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To have used someone is to have exploited them, taking advantage.

clue.text: Lacking up-to-date information from contact

parts.note: out of means from, as in made out of wood
touch is contact, as in keep in touch

explanation.surface: Someone lacking current news gets it from a contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of touch is an idiom for not knowing current developments.

clue.text: Mount attending Newmarket — name?

indicators.note: attending means being present at, so the mountain is present within these words

explanation.surface: A horse called Mount runs at Newmarket races, but what is its name?
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is an English racecourse town; the mountain sits across its last letters and the start of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily, so it is a mount.

clue.text: Technocrat ordered waterproof item of clothing

indicators.note: ordered means arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A technocrat orders a waterproof garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench coat is a belted raincoat originally worn by officers in the First World War trenches.
